premise: Acorn wants to be as big as the great trees right now; Squirrel tucks her into the soft earth before the snow, and when the spring sun comes Acorn feels a tickle in her toes — a root growing down first.
inspiration: "Great oaks from little acorns grow" (proverb) and the small-seed folk motif, turned toward patience: the first growing happens where nobody can see it.
lesson: Big things start small, and some growing happens out of sight.
learning: An acorn grows a root down into the ground first, before its shoot grows up.

en-US.title: Acorn Wants to Be a Tree
en-US.text: {acorn:enter} Acorn looked up at the two great trees. {acorn:face happy} {acorn:live talk} [excited] "I want to be big like them. Right NOW!" Along came {squirrel:enter} Squirrel, bounding. [giggles] "Right now? Big trees start small, little one. Down in the ground." {squirrel:go to acorn} So, before the first snow, Squirrel {squirrel:live bury} {sfx:pat} tucked Acorn into the soft earth, pat, pat, pat. {squirrel:hearts} Close by, {flower:enter} Flower {flower:tint #BFE3FF} shivered. "I'll wait with you," she said, and {flower:live close hold} folded up tight. {canvas:snow 0.6} Then the snowflakes came. {acorn:live wish hold} Acorn squeezed her eyes tight and wished. "Grow… grow… GROW!" But nothing happened. [softly] Not that day, and not the next. She waited all winter long. {canvas:sunshine 0.9 20s} {sfx:birds} Then one morning the sun came back and melted the snow away. {flower:live close resume} Flower opened wide. And Acorn felt a tickle in her toes. {acorn:live wish resume} [gasps] "Am I a tree?" {acorn:face surprised} {squirrel:face happy} {squirrel:live shake-head} "Not yet," said Squirrel. "That's your root, going down first. Your shoot comes up next." {acorn:face happy} {acorn:glow} Down first, then up! [softly] And for once, Acorn didn't mind waiting one little bit.

es-ES.title: Bellota quiere ser un árbol
es-ES.text: {acorn:enter} Bellota miraba los dos árboles grandes. {acorn:face happy} {acorn:live talk} [excited] —¡Yo quiero ser así de grande! ¡Ahora MISMO! Y llegó {squirrel:enter} Ardilla, dando brincos. [giggles] —¿Ahora mismo? Los árboles grandes empiezan pequeñitos, bajo tierra. {squirrel:go to acorn} Así que, antes de las primeras nieves, Ardilla {squirrel:live bury} {sfx:pat} arropó a Bellota en la tierra blanda: pom, pom, pom. {squirrel:hearts} Muy cerca, {flower:enter} Flor {flower:tint #BFE3FF} tiritaba. —Yo espero contigo —le dijo, y {flower:live close hold} se cerró bien cerradita. {canvas:snow 0.6} Y empezó a nevar. {acorn:live wish hold} Bellota apretó los ojos y pidió un deseo: —¡Crecer… crecer… CRECER! Pero no pasó nada. [softly] Ni ese día, ni el siguiente. Esperó todo el invierno. {canvas:sunshine 0.9 20s} {sfx:birds} Hasta que una mañana volvió el sol y derritió la nieve. {flower:live close resume} Flor se abrió de par en par. Y Bellota sintió cosquillas en los pies. {acorn:live wish resume} [gasps] —¿Ya soy un árbol? {acorn:face surprised} {squirrel:face happy} {squirrel:live shake-head} —Todavía no —dijo Ardilla—. Es tu raíz, que baja primero. Luego sube el tallo. {acorn:face happy} {acorn:glow} ¡Primero abajo y luego arriba! [softly] Y, por una vez, a Bellota no le importó nada esperar.
